blocks.text:
Arrive in Lima. Meet at the airport and transfer to a 3-star hotel.

Lima lies on the Pacific coast, where European colonial architecture stands alongside pre-Inca monuments. No sightseeing is scheduled after your flight, so you can rest or take a first walk on your own.
Illuminated fountain in front of Lima Cathedral at night, Peru
Lima: fountain jets and the floodlit cathedral towers

After breakfast, you set out on a guided tour.

Your first stop is **Love Park** in the Miraflores district. It features *The Kiss*, a sculpture by Peruvian artist Víctor Delfín. The park opened on 14 February 1993. Its walls and paths overlook the Pacific Ocean, and the walls are decorated with quotations about love.

You then pass through **San Isidro**, home to many of Lima’s financial institutions, on your way to the historic centre.

On the main square, you see the **Government Palace, City Hall and the Archbishop’s Palace**. The tour includes a visit to Lima Cathedral, where Francisco Pizarro, the founder of Lima, is buried. Admission is included.

Your next stop is the **Convent of Santo Domingo**. As you walk through its corridors, you learn about the history of Peru’s saints. Admission is also included.

Part of the tour is devoted to **Casa Aliaga**, one of Lima’s oldest houses. It was built in the 16th century, when the city was founded, on the foundations of an Inca pyramid. Descendants of the Spanish conquistador Captain Aliaga still live there.

The house has 66 rooms, of which only some are open to visitors. The interiors feature paintings of the Cusco School, carved furniture and antique chests.

At **18:00**, the Magic Water Tour begins. You visit a complex of **12 computer-controlled fountains**. Some of the jets reach approximately **80 metres**.

Return to the hotel after the evening programme.
Peruvian flag above the square and Lima Cathedral, Peru
